statement.excerpt: If NVIDIA doesn’t solve its cooling problem — and solve it well — its customers will undoubtedly encounter thermal throttling, where the chip reduces speed in order to avoid causing permanent damage.

from_speaker: If NVIDIA doesn’t solve its cooling problem
its customers will undoubtedly encounter thermal throttling
our_interpretation: The context concerns Blackwell data-center racks, particularly GB200 configurations, rather than gaming GPUs or DGX Spark.
The antecedent is inadequate rack cooling persisting into customer deployment. It need not mean that NVIDIA can never fix the problem.
Thermal throttling means an observed heat-triggered reduction in chip clocks or speed. Delayed shipments, leaks, shutdowns, and interconnect failures are not substitutes.
The reference to deployments in early 2025 supplies context, not an explicit deadline for the conditional forecast.

criteria.contradiction_condition: Sufficient customer operating evidence shows that the identified unresolved cooling condition persists under the relevant sustained loads without the predicted thermal throttling.
